name: Charlie Starr
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember painting a bedroom before I knew who its owner was.” People around the downtown fountain know Charlie by a small Monday habit. Charlie keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I painted the spare room blue. He called it a color for a nursery and I nearly sent him packing.
appearance: Charlie has two dimples that appear only with a full smile. Look for a long plait tucked inside the collar. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a pale blue work shirt with a watch on a cracked leather band. In conversation Charlie takes off the watch before a long conversation.
personality: Charlie is fond of ambitious ideas and deeply suspicious of grand openings. The question Charlie asks at any launch is who has the keys for cleaning up a month later.
agenda: To finish the blue room on terms the returning parent can accept.
family: Rene Mott is Charlie’s cousin. Charlie can always ask for five minutes alone. Rene asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *An unfinished atlas*, Rene says, “My hand shook the day I ruined a school register with too much water.”
connections: Sonia Garza. Preparing a bedroom competes with the guest's own need for occasional space in the house.

reactions.situation: A sibling leaves the room during the welcome dinner
reactions.response: Charlie leaves the departing sibling room to get out without turning supper into a vote.

reactions.situation: The last bus leaves while an elderly stranger is still crossing toward it
reactions.response: Charlie asks the stranger who will be expecting them, then helps find a way to tell that person.

reactions.response: Charlie accepts only after finding out whether the person doing the regular work can come too.
